note: Self-assessed status with evidence. audit_score is copied from audit/REQUIREMENTS_MATRIX.md and only the auditor changes it.

capabilities.title: IDE shell: project tree, tabs, panels, palette, keyboard
capabilities.note: Tree, tabs, panels, palette, status bar, F6 regions, small-screen fallback (ADR-0013). axe-core scan only; no screen-reader session.

capabilities.title: Blockly editing with deterministic generation and block-to-source maps
capabilities.note: Block id -> IR path -> C/assembly lines (source_map artifact) -> addresses (DWARF line table), saved per build; generated code unchanged (ADR-0015).

capabilities.title: C editor with language services
capabilities.note: Offline completion (portable ABI only), hover, signature help, F12 into a generated prg32.h, live diagnostics at exact ranges that mirror validate_c_source, resident-only calls, compiler messages without paths (ADR-0014). No C type or scope analysis: deeper errors come from the compiler. After every save the real PRG32 compiler checks the saved, validated source in the build sandbox (nothing kept) and its messages join Problems at their lines (ADR-0014); compiler errors from Compile now reach their line too (<build>/ paths).

capabilities.title: RISC-V assembly editor with language services
capabilities.note: RV32IMC + Zicsr instruction, register and allowed-directive completion, PRG32 call help with the ilp32 calling convention, labels and F12, live diagnostics at exact ranges mirroring validate_asm_source plus unknown instructions/registers (ADR-0014). Operand types are not checked. After every save the real PRG32 compiler checks the saved, validated source in the build sandbox (nothing kept) and its messages join Problems at their lines (ADR-0014); compiler errors from Compile now reach their line too (<build>/ paths).

capabilities.title: Versioned project model, archive, history, migrations
capabilities.note: Autosave and conflict-safe saves done (ADR-0017); no project search and no automatic merge of concurrent edits (the student chooses). New Project offers Blocks, C or assembly; C and assembly start from the starter game turned into code (/api/starters).

capabilities.title: Blocks, C and assembly build real PRG32 cartridges
capabilities.note: Real-build tests need the PRG32 toolchain and skip without it. tools/reproduce_toolchain_checks.py runs them with Docker only: on 2026-10-21 (kit b547d82) check_build built Blocks (as C and as assembly), Advanced C and handwritten assembly for both targets, the fixtures rebuilt byte for byte, and 112 toolchain tests passed (docs/evidence/toolchain); the same cartridges, built on macOS, have identical SHA-256.

capabilities.title: Isolated, reproducible builds with provenance
capabilities.note: bubblewrap escape tests run only where bubblewrap works (Linux container, CI).

capabilities.title: Browser runtime is the pinned PRG32-QT core
capabilities.note: Reference: PRG32-QT prg32qt-headless and native core, revision in static/wasm/BUILD.json.

capabilities.title: Browser host: framebuffer, input, timing, audio, offline
capabilities.note: Framebuffer/input/timing/offline covered; sound is the firmware's audio engine played as PCM (ADR-0021).

capabilities.title: Eight SID-like voices with independent ADSR
capabilities.note: The browser core runs the PRG32 firmware's own audio engine (ADR-0021): 8 voices, SID-like synth with filter, independent ADSR, samples, tracker; checked against the contract's formulas on a toolchain-built 8-voice fixture. The real firmware in QEMU renders the same samples between events, and with the proposed SDK patch the console check's whole soundtrack (8-voice chord, envelopes, hard left/right, silences) is equal sample for sample (docs/evidence/qemu-audio). No console recording yet (docs/hardware_audio_check.md).

capabilities.title: Stereo audio and cross-runtime sample parity
capabilities.note: Stereo PCM from the firmware's mixer: WebAssembly, native and PRG32-QT with the proposed patch (firmware audio by default, real output device checked) are bit-identical on the conformance fixture and the console check. One scheduling boundary (ADR-0021 frame clock): audio calls take effect at their frame's start, N x 33 ms, so effects sound from buffer floor(N x 33 / 20). With the proposed SDK patch the QEMU firmware equals the browser core over the whole recording in three runs each: console check 546/546 buffers, conformance 348/348, same SHA-256 (PRG32-QT with its patch too). Patches proposed as riscv-prg32/PRG32#45, #46 and riscv-prg32/PRG32-QT#1 (open, not merged). Not yet: the patches merged upstream, and a console capture (procedure, comparator and evidence check ready).

capabilities.title: AudioStudio instruments, sound effects and soundtracks
capabilities.note: AudioStudio page parallel to Sprite Lab: 8 voice instruments with ADSR, sound effects, an 8-row soundtrack grid, WAV samples; previewed through the PRG32 engine; one versioned audio_studio asset per project (expected_version, 409, quotas, ownership); named blocks become fixed instrument/track numbers in the generated C and assembly; the AUD0 block is packed deterministically into the cartridge build; archive, copy and export carry the samples. Soundtrack timing fixed to the tracker's wait-after deltas (13766c9 played notes one gap early). Keyboard-only, archive and Compile paths checked in a real browser; the console check cartridge is built from an AudioStudio project. No screen-reader session or console recording yet.

capabilities.title: Obsolete buzzer removal
capabilities.note: Kit side complete: refused in C and assembly, obsolete-only in the language index, silent and counted for old cartridges, a repository-wide guard. The SDK retirement is a tested patch (docs/upstream/prg32-sdk-retire-buzzer.patch: ABI 1.7, slots 5/7/8 kept and silent, the 1.6 hash compatible, no public declaration, examples migrated; SDK tests 89 passed); the canonical SDK still exports the buzzer until it is merged.

capabilities.title: Instruction, over, out stepping
capabilities.note: Dedicated RV32C fixture (tests/fixtures/debug/compressed.S) steps 2- and 4-byte instructions alike in WebAssembly and natively; Step line/Next block over calls.

capabilities.title: Breakpoints
capabilities.note: Address, C/assembly line and Blockly block breakpoints, with optional conditions checked when they hit; remembered per cartridge.

capabilities.title: Registers, memory, disassembly, CSR, stack, watches
capabilities.note: CSR view = the counters the core implements (cycle/time/instret + high halves); no other CSRs exist in the core. Stack view = words around sp.

capabilities.title: C locals, call stack, watches (DWARF); active Blockly block
capabilities.note: DWARF from a -g build with an identical cartridge; locals optimised out at -Os are labelled; inlined functions are frames 'inlined into' their caller (no variables shown); breakpoints persist per project and follow their code across regeneration, with enable/disable; handwritten assembly gets lines, labels and an ra-based caller.

capabilities.title: Guest policies and IndexedDB guest projects
capabilities.note: Policy local/off (PRG32_GUEST_MODE); IndexedDB guest games with capacity message, export/import, safe clearing, legacy migration and move-to-account after sign-in (ADR-0017). Temporary server storage for guests deliberately not offered. ADR-0023: the full kit (IDE, Sprite Lab, AudioStudio, Player) opens without an account by default; guest data in IndexedDB v2, stateless guest API for code and sound; build, publish and classes need a sign-in.

capabilities.title: Registered storage: ownership, history, quotas, autosave, retention
capabilities.note: Ownership, history, conflict-safe versions, autosave, quotas, retention (trash, builds, orphan folders) and deprovisioning (ADR-0016/0017). No automatic deletion of accounts.

capabilities.title: OIDC with PKCE, issuer+subject identity
capabilities.note: Authorization Code + PKCE (S256), single-use state and nonce, ID token signature (RS256/PS256/ES256, JWKS rotation), iss/aud/azp/exp/iat; accounts by issuer+subject, never joined by email (ADR-0016). In-process provider tests plus an opt-in live suite against Keycloak 26.0.7 (docs/identity_live_testing.md), run 2026-10-21 through tools/run_live_suites.py: 9 passed (docs/evidence/live/2026-10-21); no institutional tenant run recorded.

capabilities.title: Multiple admin-configured IdPs, claim mapping, recovery
capabilities.note: Admin-configured providers (secret by reference), claim -> academic role mapping, allowed domains, explicit linking/unlinking as recovery. No SCIM (just-in-time accounts, admin deprovisioning); logout is local only and says so (ADR-0016 amendment).

capabilities.title: Scoped student/TA/teacher/publisher/admin capabilities
capabilities.note: Global roles shared with CartridgeStore unchanged; kit-only academic roles (student/teacher/facilitator/service) and class memberships give read-only supervision; scoped, expiring API tokens.

capabilities.title: Shared accounts with CartridgeStore
capabilities.note: Shared users checked against CartridgeStore's own code in the store-contract CI job (disposable, in-process); no production Store. Live (2026-10-21, tests/test_sso_live.py, CI Store job): the kit as an HTTP server and a throwaway CartridgeStore process share users and roles, sign in both ways with one-time tickets, and a publisher's bundle reaches the Store with a one-time API ticket while reused, forged or sign-in tickets are refused; the Store checks sign-in only, so the kit's publisher check is the authorization.

capabilities.title: OneDrive

capabilities.note: Shared versioned contract (ADR-0018) checked against the Store's own code and a disposable loopback Store in CI. Store gaps (duplicate pending id/version, tokens without expiry) are closed on the kit side (one bundle per version, token age limit) and proposed to CartridgeStore; not yet changed there.

capabilities.title: PRG32-QT delivery
capabilities.note: Delivery recorded 2026-10-21 (docs/evidence/delivery/2026-10-21-prg32qt): canonical PRG32-QT f6d80ad stored, started and drew five kit cartridges (Blocks as C and as assembly, Advanced C, handwritten assembly, the console audio check) through its web API, with screenshots; their SHA-256 equal the Docker-built ones. Through the API, not the desktop Import menu clicked by a person.

capabilities.note: docs/privacy/: field-level record of processing (every column), proposed roles and legal bases, retention, processors and transfers, children/DPIA/DPO screening, notices with recorded versions, rights workflows (export, register with deadlines, restriction, erasure across tables, folders, files, cloud tokens, audit pseudonyms, backups re-apply), Article 32 review, breach playbook and a technical rehearsal (ADR-0022).
